question: What is the main focus of substantive conflict?

options.A: General dislike of a uniform policy
options.B: Personal emotions and ego
options.C: Tasks, facts, and procedures
options.D: Hatred between two coworkers

explanation: Substantive conflict focuses purely on work-related ideas and methods, not personal feelings.

question: Which of the following is NOT a common barrier to client-centered drug administration in hospitals?

options.A: Institutional time pressures during busy medication passes
options.B: Heavy workloads and short nursing staff numbers
options.C: Having too many clinical pharmacists available on every shift
options.D: Language differences between the nurse and the patient

explanation: Having more clinical pharmacists actually helps improve medication safety rather than acting as a barrier to care. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T3#GNS125_U3_T3_h7)

question: What color do Gram-positive bacteria show up as under the microscope after a Gram stain?

options.A: Blue
options.B: Green
options.C: Pink
options.D: Purple

explanation: Gram-positive bacteria have thick cell walls that proudly trap that bright purple crystal violet dye. Easy to remember: P for Positive and Purple!

question: A patient is upset after getting the wrong test. What is the best way to talk to them first?

options.A: Tell them to speak only to the legal department outside the hospital
options.B: Acknowledge their frustration, listen to their concerns, and explain the next steps
options.C: Tell them that mistakes happen to everyone and they should not worry
options.D: Threaten to discharge them if they continue asking questions

explanation: Validating their feelings builds trust! Letting them know you hear them is a core part of professional nursing care.

question: What is the main purpose of a tally sheet during a busy immunization outreach?

options.A: To record the home address and phone number of each mother
options.B: To write detailed medical histories for every child present
options.C: To quickly count services rendered without writing full names
options.D: To calculate the total financial cost of the vaccines

explanation: Exactly! Tally sheets let us use quick tick marks to keep track of patient volume during busy clinic hours without slowing down to write long names.

question: What is the primary reason nurses 'cohort' patients in a hospital ward?

options.A: To make it easier for doctors to prescribe the exact same medication
options.B: To ensure that patients with different diseases share recovery rooms
options.C: To group patients with the same infection together to contain transmission
options.D: To reduce the total number of nursing staff required on the ward

explanation: Cohorting means putting patients with the exact same bug in one designated area so they don't spread it to uninfected patients.

question: Which of these is a great advocacy action a nurse can take to support community inclusion?

options.A: Encouraging patients to remain indoors to avoid public ridicule
options.B: Focusing exclusively on medication adherence during home visits
options.C: Educating local leaders and connecting families with welfare resources
options.D: Restricting community nursing visits to clinic grounds only

explanation: You've got it! Nurses act as wonderful bridges by teaching the community and linking families to helpful social resources.

question: What percentage of total hospital waste is generally made up of non-hazardous general waste?

options.A: Nearly 95 percent
options.B: About 75 to 80 percent
options.C: Exactly 50 percent
options.D: Around 10 to 15 percent

explanation: The majority of hospital waste is general refuse that poses no direct health risk and can be handled like normal household trash. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T5#GNS122_U5_T5_h1)

question: What is a key responsibility of the psychiatric nurse in continuing care?

options.A: Managing hospital finances and staff payroll budgets
options.B: Observing mental status and evaluating medication side effects
options.C: Prescribing brand new antipsychotic drugs independently
options.D: Diagnosing rare surgical disorders in the community

explanation: Nurses closely monitor how the patient is doing mentally and check for any troublesome reactions to prescribed drugs. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T5#GNS314_U4_T5_h3)

question: How often should you check the patient's breathing during the early phase of steam therapy?

options.A: Every four hours
options.B: Only when the patient rings the bell
options.C: Every fifteen minutes
options.D: Once every shift

explanation: Checking frequently at the start ensures the patient is taking in the moisture well and their breathing is improving.

question: Why is daily weight tracking so important for a patient taking oral prednisone?

options.A: It helps catch fluid retention and rapid water weight gain early.
options.B: It calculates the exact dose needed for the next day.
options.C: It proves the patient is absorbing pills through the stomach.
options.D: It ensures the patient is following a workout routine.

explanation: Spot on! Steroids cause the body to hold onto salt and water, making daily weigh-ins a great way to spot fluid overload early.

question: A nurse draws up the wrong dose of insulin, but catches the mistake before giving it to the patient. What is this called?

options.A: A systemic failure
options.B: An adverse event
options.C: A sentinel event
options.D: A near miss

explanation: Spotting the mistake before the injection means no harm was done. That's a classic near miss—phew!

question: Why can't we use very heavy weights with skin traction?

options.A: Heavy weights will damage the skin and slip off
options.B: Skin traction requires a surgical operating room
options.C: Heavy weights make the patient fall asleep faster
options.D: Skin bones cannot support heavy metal devices

explanation: Skin is tough, but it's not made to carry heavy loads! Too much weight will cause blisters, tears, or just slip right out of the straps.

question: What is the main goal of civil service rules for government workers?

options.A: To replace the professional nursing curriculum set by the council
options.B: To provide a standard framework for employment and administrative conduct
options.C: To dictate the specific clinical medications nurses can prescribe
options.D: To determine the personal income tax rates for civil servants

explanation: Civil service rules are simply the workplace guidelines that keep public institutions organized. They tell everyone what is expected regarding job terms and daily conduct!

question: A patient in the ER has a fast heart rate, cool sweaty skin, and slow capillary refill. What do these signs tell you?

options.A: They are simply recovering from light exercise
options.B: The brain and heart are getting plenty of oxygen
options.C: Poor blood flow and possible shock
options.D: The nervous system is just overactive

explanation: Spot on! The body pulls blood away from the skin to protect vital organs like the heart and brain when blood volume is low. Classic signs of shock!

question: Why are helper T-cells considered the master coordinators of the immune system?

options.A: They physically swallow large bacteria and digest them inside stomach acid.
options.B: They create a hard physical barrier around damaged skin to stop bleeding.
options.C: They release chemical signals that activate both B-cells and other T-cells.
options.D: They turn into red blood cells when the body suffers from severe anemia.

explanation: Helper T-cells act like military commanders, sending chemical messages to rally both B-cells and other T-cells into action.

question: What is the main health benefit of early breast milk (colostrum) for a newborn?

options.A: It gives them high dietary fiber
options.B: It stops jaundice from happening
options.C: It acts as a sleeping pill
options.D: It provides heavy antibodies and protein to protect the tummy

explanation: Colostrum is liquid gold! It is packed with protective antibodies (like IgA) that line the baby's gut to fight off early germs.

question: What is the highest possible value for a correlation coefficient?

options.A: zero
options.B: plus or minus 100
options.C: plus or minus 1.00
options.D: infinity

explanation: Well done! Correlation numbers always stay neatly between -1.00 and +1.00.

question: Why might a nurse researcher choose an observational checklist instead of a patient questionnaire?

options.A: Patients prefer being watched over writing answers
options.B: What people say they do can differ from their actual actions
options.C: Observational checklists are much cheaper to print
options.D: Questionnaires cannot be used in a hospital setting

explanation: Direct observation captures real behavior, avoiding the bias or forgetfulness that comes with self-reporting. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T21#GNS224_U1_T21_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a core principle of a Drug Revolving Fund?

options.A: Maintaining strict financial accountability and transparency
options.B: Selling pharmaceuticals at affordable prices to patients
options.C: Maximizing high profit margins for hospital expansion
options.D: Ensuring constant availability of essential medicines

explanation: A DRF is not a business meant to chase huge profits! It focuses on cost-recovery to keep medicines affordable and available for everyday patients.

question: How should a nurse respond when community members attribute mental illness to spiritual causes?

options.A: Refuse to treat anyone in that community
options.B: Agree that hospitals are useless and refer everyone to shrines
options.C: Mock their beliefs and insist only on Western medicine
options.D: Acknowledge their perspective while respectfully integrating mental health education

explanation: Respecting local worldviews builds trust, allowing nurses to gently introduce helpful mental health concepts alongside traditional beliefs. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T7#GNS314_U4_T7_h5)

question: Why is it important to use local languages and traditional communication channels for immunization campaigns?

options.A: It prevents the government from spending money on printed books
options.B: It is required to qualify for international medical grants
options.C: It stops people from visiting traditional bone setters
options.D: It ensures the message is clearly understood and trusted by residents

explanation: Using familiar languages and traditional methods like town criers breaks down communication barriers and reduces fear. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T71#GNS214_U1_T71_h3)

question: According to safety science, what is usually at the root of most medical errors in hospitals?

options.A: They are completely unavoidable in modern hospitals.
options.B: They occur only in surgical departments.
options.C: They are caused entirely by careless staff members.
options.D: They usually stem from complex system failures.

explanation: Modern safety studies show that errors happen because work processes or systems are flawed—not just because someone was careless. We fix systems to help nurses succeed!

question: Why is it important to speak up and report physical discomfort early on?

options.A: It guarantees an immediate promotion to head nurse
options.B: It allows management to reduce the staff member's salary
options.C: It prevents minor aches from turning into disabling injuries
options.D: It is required before a nurse can take a lunch break

explanation: Exactly! Catching little aches and pains early means you can fix them before they turn into major health problems. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h8)

question: Why is it important to remove loose rugs from the home of a patient with dementia?

options.A: To keep the house looking neat for visitors
options.B: To stop the patient from eating fabric fibers
options.C: To prevent dangerous tripping and fall accidents
options.D: To reduce dust allergies in the living room

explanation: Safety first! Loose rugs are sneaky slip hazards for older adults whose balance and spatial awareness are already affected.

question: What is the single most common cause of chronic renal failure here in Nigeria?

options.A: Congenital bladder defects
options.B: Polycystic kidney disease
options.C: Acute bacterial pneumonia
options.D: Chronic hypertension

explanation: Great clinical insight to carry into practice! High blood pressure puts constant, hard pressure on the tiny blood vessels in the kidneys, making it the leading cause of renal failure in our region.

question: What is an epidemiological 'reservoir'?

options.A: The natural habitat where an infectious agent normally lives and multiplies
options.B: The chemical disinfectant applied to counter harmful pathogens
options.C: The protective antibodies built up inside a patient's bloodstream
options.D: The medical equipment used to sterilize hospital surgical instruments

explanation: Think of a reservoir as home sweet home for the germ—where it hangs out, grows, and thrives over time.

question: Why is keeping a consistent meal schedule so important for a diabetic patient taking insulin?

options.A: To match the timing of food intake with peak insulin action and prevent low blood sugar
options.B: To ensure the digestive enzymes are secreted in exact equal amounts daily
options.C: To guarantee that the liver stores excess fat in safe tissue compartments
options.D: To prevent the patient from experiencing chronic kidney failure symptoms

explanation: When insulin is active in the body but food is delayed, blood sugar can crash dangerously low (hypoglycemia). Regular meals keep them safe and balanced.

question: A hospital unit arranges all high-alert drugs in the exact same alphabetical order in every medication room. What safety design principle is this?

options.A: Complex redundancy
options.B: Punitive discipline
options.C: Manual override
options.D: Standardization

explanation: Exactly! Keeping supplies and medications laid out identically across multiple units prevents confusion and helps nurses find what they need quickly and safely.

question: What does the legal principle 'if it is not documented, it was not done' mean for a community health nurse?

options.A: Unrecorded care has no legal proof in a court or disciplinary hearing
options.B: Nurses must write down every single word a client speaks all day
options.C: Clients can refuse to pay if their chart lacks a doctor's stamp
options.D: Verbal reports to relatives completely replace written case notes

explanation: In legal investigations, courts rely solely on written records; unrecorded interventions cannot be proven to have taken place. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T6#GNS324_U2_T6_h2)

question: Which model looks at behaviour change as stepping through different stages, like thinking about it, then finally taking action?

options.A: Transtheoretical Model
options.B: Epidemiological Triangle
options.C: Health Belief Model
options.D: Germ Theory of Disease

explanation: Spot on! The Transtheoretical Model helps us understand that change takes time and happens in steady steps.

question: What is special about the mechanoreceptors sitting right near the surface of the skin?

options.A: They lack nerve fiber connections
options.B: They have small receptive fields for fine detail
options.C: They respond exclusively to extreme temperatures
options.D: They only detect deep, heavy pressure

explanation: Spot on! Because their receptive fields are small, superficial receptors help your brain pinpoint exact touches and feel fine textures.

question: What is the main goal of stress management for someone with neurasthenia?

options.A: Eliminating all life responsibilities permanently
options.B: Teaching the patient how to ignore family members
options.C: Helping the patient identify triggers and use healthier coping skills
options.D: Prescribing strong sedative medications

explanation: Spot on! Helping patients spot their stressors and handle them better stops total burnout before it happens. You are learning real clinical skills!

question: What is the medical term for infective bone disease?

options.A: Osteoarthritis
options.B: Osteoporosis
options.C: Osteomyelitis
options.D: Osteomalacia

explanation: Osteomyelitis is the specific term used to describe an infection and inflammation of the bone and bone marrow. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T17#GNS222_U1_T17_h1)

question: Why is it so important to involve local community members when planning a health program?

options.A: It ensures cultural acceptance and long-term program sustainability
options.B: It eliminates the need for professional nursing staff entirely
options.C: It guarantees immediate federal funding for hospital construction
options.D: It prevents any future outbreaks of infectious diseases

explanation: Brilliant! When a community helps design their own health programs, they take ownership of them, and the project lasts much longer because it respects their local culture.

question: Why is it so important to report a disease outbreak quickly in your community?

options.A: It guarantees free medical treatment for all citizens
options.B: It stops patients from visiting traditional healers
options.C: It helps health agencies spot unusual disease patterns early
options.D: It reduces the cost of prescription drugs in pharmacies

explanation: Spotting cases early gives health teams the heads-up they need to track trends and stop epidemics in their tracks. You're building solid public health sense!

question: A patient with a fresh neck injury suddenly has dangerously low blood pressure and zero reflexes. What is this temporary condition called?

options.A: Renal failure
options.B: Cerebral edema
options.C: Tetraplegic fever
options.D: Spinal shock

explanation: Spot on! Spinal shock happens right after a severe spinal cord injury. The cord basically goes to 'sleep' temporarily, causing a sudden loss of all reflexes and muscle tone below the injury site.

question: When is the best time to document patient care and assessments?

options.A: Before performing the actual physical assessment
options.B: Immediately after the care is provided
options.C: Whenever the head nurse requests a chart review
options.D: At the end of the 12-hour shift from memory

explanation: Always chart right away! Waiting until the end of a long, tiring shift makes it easy to forget important details.

question: Why do communicable diseases spread so quickly in crowded IDP camps?

options.A: Close living quarters and poor sanitation facilities
options.B: Frequent distribution of expired food supplies
options.C: Lack of available traditional herbal remedies
options.D: Mandatory daily group physical exercise routines

explanation: When people live very close together without proper toilets or clean water, infections spread easily from person to person.

question: Which gene mutations are most strongly linked to a higher risk of ovarian cancer?

options.A: BRCA1 and BRCA2
options.B: HER2 and KRAS
options.C: TP53 and EGFR
options.D: APC and MLH1

explanation: Spot on. Inherited mutations in the BRCA1 and BRCA2 genes significantly increase a woman's lifetime chance of developing both breast and ovarian cancers.

question: Why is mixing local herbal mixtures with modern hospital drugs a hidden danger during self-medication?

options.A: Herbal mixtures are always chemically identical to factory-made pills
options.B: Herbs always taste too bitter to swallow with tablets
options.C: Unregulated herbs may contain hidden drugs that cause harmful interactions
options.D: Modern drugs completely destroy the healing power of leaves

explanation: You got it! Local mixtures often have active chemical ingredients that clash unpredictably with your hospital prescription.

question: What crucial details must always be included on a community health referral form?

options.A: The financial salary grade of the attending nurse
options.B: The personal home phone number of the village chief
options.C: Assessment findings and initial care given
options.D: A complete inventory of clinic furniture

explanation: You got it! The receiving hospital needs to know your assessment findings and what emergency treatments you already started before they arrived.

question: When teaching a patient about nutrition, which factor must you always keep in mind?

options.A: The brand name of hospital bed sheets
options.B: The specific color of the nursing uniform
options.C: Economic background and food access
options.D: The manufacturer of the IV infusion pump

explanation: Always consider what the patient can afford and find in their local market. A great meal plan is useless if they can't afford to buy the ingredients!

question: Which common bacterium is most often linked to duodenal ulcers?

options.A: Escherichia coli
options.B: Pseudomonas aeruginosa
options.C: Helicobacter pylori
options.D: Staphylococcus aureus

explanation: Spot on! Helicobacter pylori (or H. pylori) is a tough little spiral bacterium that sneaks under the protective mucus layer of the stomach and duodenum, causing sores.

question: What happens when homeostatic failure is left untreated for too long?

options.A: Vital organs begin to shut down and shock can occur
options.B: The patient enters a state of deep relaxation
options.C: The body automatically fixes itself without any help
options.D: Blood pressure rises to a very safe level

explanation: Spot on. If the body's regulatory systems stay broken down, tissues are starved of oxygen, which can quickly lead to organ failure and shock.

question: If a patient has an infection causing nausea, vomiting, and watery stool, what is the most important thing to watch out for?

options.A: Sudden muscle hypertrophy
options.B: Elevated blood pressure
options.C: Fluid volume deficit
options.D: High red blood cell count

explanation: Exactly right! Vomiting and diarrhea drain body fluids fast, putting the patient at high risk for dehydration.

question: What does an 'in-kind' donation mean when talking about healthcare support?

options.A: Exchanging foreign currency at local black-market rates
options.B: Providing free land ownership titles to international aid workers
options.C: Supplying physical goods like medications and equipment instead of cash
options.D: Paying hospital staff salaries exclusively through electronic bank transfers

explanation: In-kind support simply means giving actual, tangible medical supplies and equipment rather than handing over raw cash.

question: What is the main purpose of a hospital budget?

options.A: Hiding financial losses from the external government auditors
options.B: Determining which nurses receive promotions based on seniority
options.C: Planning how expected revenue will be spent over a specific period
options.D: Punishing departments that fail to meet their monthly patient targets

explanation: Think of a budget as your financial roadmap! It helps a hospital map out expected income and plan expenses for a set timeframe.

question: Which of these is a clear example of a psychosocial hazard at work?

options.A: Bullying and harassment from a supervisor
options.B: A cut from an unsterilized scalpel
options.C: Lifting a heavy patient without help
options.D: Breathing in toxic welding fumes

explanation: Psychosocial hazards deal with workplace relationships, job pressure, and emotional stresses like bullying or heavy emotional demands.

question: How does the parasympathetic system help control your urinary bladder?

options.A: It tightens all sphincters so you never pee
options.B: It relaxes the bladder wall to hold more urine
options.C: It contracts the bladder wall to help you pass urine
options.D: It has no role in urinary control

explanation: Parasympathetic stimulation tells the bladder wall (detrusor muscle) to squeeze and the internal sphincter to relax so urine can flow out. Excellent nursing knowledge!

question: What is the primary function of the sensory strip located in the parietal lobe?

options.A: Processing touch, pain, and temperature
options.B: Regulating heartbeat and breathing
options.C: Controlling voluntary muscle movement
options.D: Interpreting visual images and colors

explanation: The sensory strip receives incoming touch and temperature signals from different parts of the body. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T23#GNS211_U3_T23_h3)

question: Why do healthcare workers often check serum prealbumin instead of albumin to track recent nutritional changes?

options.A: It measures total body fat instead of protein
options.B: It has a shorter half-life and responds faster
options.C: It is much cheaper to run in any lab
options.D: It never changes during an infection

explanation: Prealbumin leaves the body quicker, meaning it shows recent nutrition improvements or drops much faster than albumin.

question: How do poverty and cultural barriers team up to worsen pregnancy outcomes in tough settings?

options.A: They cause immediate cessation of all hormonal activities
options.B: They automatically increase the biological rate of twin pregnancies
options.C: They eliminate the need for community health nursing outreaches
options.D: They delay timely care-seeking and restrict access to skilled birth attendants

explanation: Spot on. When money is tight or cultural beliefs hold sway, women often reach the hospital too late, leading to avoidable emergencies.

question: What is the very first thing you should do if you accidentally get poked by a needle?

options.A: Take a strong dose of broad antibiotics
options.B: Apply a tight tourniquet above the elbow
options.C: Fill out an incident report form for HR
options.D: Wash the puncture site with soap and water

explanation: Quickly washing the spot with soap and water helps flush away germs before they can enter your bloodstream.

question: During a building collapse, a nurse finds a victim who is unresponsive, not breathing even after opening the airway, and has no pulse. What triage tag should they get?

options.A: Green (Walking Wounded)
options.B: Red (Immediate)
options.C: Yellow (Delayed)
options.D: Black (Expectant / Deceased)

explanation: This is a tough call in mass casualty triage, but a black tag is used when injuries are so severe that resuscitation is impossible, allowing us to focus on survivors.

question: A community health nurse organizes a blood pressure screening in the marketplace. What level of prevention is this?

options.A: Secondary prevention
options.B: Primary prevention
options.C: Tertiary prevention
options.D: Terminal prevention

explanation: Screenings are classified as secondary prevention because they catch health problems early when treatment is most effective. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T6#GNS225_U1_T6_h3)

question: How can the government best tackle the problem of nurses refusing postings to remote rural clinics due to poor living conditions?

options.A: Closing down all rural clinics and building more hospitals in the capital city
options.B: Firing all nurses who refuse urban postings without investigation
options.C: Removing nurses entirely from the primary healthcare system
options.D: Offering rural hardship allowances and improved housing for health workers

explanation: Providing financial incentives and safe housing makes it much easier and fairer for health workers to serve in remote areas.

question: Which set of symptoms in a postpartum mother is a strong warning sign of impending eclampsia (seizures)?

options.A: Severe headache, blurred vision, and upper tummy (epigastric) pain
options.B: Dry mouth, joint stiffness, and mild fatigue
options.C: Frequent urination, extreme thirst, and itchy skin
options.D: Cough, chest pain, and difficulty breathing

explanation: Keep your eyes open for these head and tummy warning signs! They tell you severe pre-eclampsia might be progressing into dangerous seizures.

question: What is the primary goal of homeostasis in the human body?

options.A: Maintaining a stable internal environment
options.B: Speeding up cellular reproduction
options.C: Increasing muscle mass during exercise
options.D: Preventing all exposure to external bacteria

explanation: Homeostasis keeps vital internal conditions like temperature, blood pressure, and chemical balance within a safe, stable range. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of a problem statement in a research proposal?

options.A: Convinces the reader that a specific issue requires study
options.B: Lists the exact financial cost of the research project
options.C: Provides a complete list of all hospital staff members
options.D: Summarizes the final results found after data collection

explanation: A problem statement points out the exact gap or trouble in current clinical practice that your research is going to help fix.

question: Which of these is a structural (physical) part of a community?

options.A: General trust among local neighbors
options.B: The overall happiness of the population
options.C: The speed of municipal emergency response
options.D: Geographical location and housing conditions

explanation: Great job! The physical structure refers to what you can actually see and map out, like houses, roads, and the location itself.

question: Why are primary healthcare facilities so important for reproductive health in Nigeria?

options.A: They exclusively handle complex surgical procedures
options.B: They are where most rural Nigerians seek initial medical care
options.C: They are fully funded by international donors without local input
options.D: They provide free medications for all chronic illnesses

explanation: Primary healthcare centers are right at the grassroots level. They are usually the very first place everyday people in rural areas go when they need medical help, making them lifesavers!

question: What is the main difference between normal grief and complicated grief?

options.A: Normal grief requires heavy psychiatric medication
options.B: Normal grief has no sadness, only anger and frustration
options.C: Complicated grief remains intense and paralyzing for six months or longer
options.D: Complicated grief only happens after sudden accidental deaths

explanation: While normal grief slowly softens over time, complicated grief stays severe and keeps a person from functioning well past the six-month mark.

question: In community health, why do leaders rely more on personal trust than strict job titles?

options.A: Formal authority only works inside large urban teaching hospitals
options.B: Community members do not respect official government titles
options.C: Volunteers and local leaders answer to community norms, not job descriptions
options.D: Health nurses are not allowed to give direct orders in villages

explanation: Since most people helping out in the community aren't clocking in as direct employees, building genuine trust and good relationships is key to getting things done. Great job thinking this through!

question: What is a common dietary practice rooted in traditional African indigenous beliefs?

options.A: Total exclusion of all cooked vegetables from the diet
options.B: Consuming only imported foods during sacred ceremonies
options.C: Mandatory fasting for forty consecutive days each year
options.D: Avoiding specific foods that serve as family or clan totems

explanation: Many indigenous African traditions practice food taboos, avoiding certain plants or animals that connect to their ancestral clan totems.

question: Which of these is an example of quantitative clinical data?

options.A: Monthly count of medication administration errors
options.B: Handwritten notes from a shift handover meeting
options.C: Subjective feedback about hospital meal quality
options.D: Patient narrative descriptions of their pain experience

explanation: Remember, quantitative data has to do with quantities and numbers! Counting how many medication errors happened in a month gives you hard numbers.

question: What should the nurse do immediately after using an instrument during a home visit?

options.A: Return it straight into the clean section of the bag
options.B: Give it to the family members to wash later
options.C: Place it on the bare floor next to the patient's bed
options.D: Keep it separated and clean it before storing it away

explanation: Used equipment must never mix with clean supplies and requires proper cleaning and disinfection before going back into the bag. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T11#GNS225_U2_T11_h3)

question: What happens if a nurse wipes a disinfectant off a bedside table the very second after spraying it?

options.A: The chemical fails to achieve its required contact time, reducing germ kill rates
options.B: The active ingredients crystallize and become more potent over the next hour
options.C: The surface becomes completely sterile due to the sudden mechanical pressure
options.D: The disinfectant works faster because friction replaces chemical dwell time

explanation: Disinfectants need a little time to sit wet on a surface to work their magic. If you wipe it off instantly, the germs survive!

question: What is the primary function of an enteric coating on a tablet?

options.A: To resist stomach acid and dissolve in the intestine
options.B: To speed up absorption directly in the stomach
options.C: To allow the pill to be easily crushed into powder
options.D: To make the pill taste sweet for children

explanation: Enteric coatings protect drugs from stomach acid and protect the stomach lining from harsh medications by dissolving further down in the gut. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T7#GNS125_U2_T7_h2)

question: What is a major benefit of using indirect learning experiences (like simulations) in nursing school?

options.A: They are always more expensive to run than actual bedside teaching
options.B: They completely replace the need for any clinical hospital rotations
options.C: They provide safe environments to explore complex scenarios without harming patients
options.D: They eliminate all forms of student evaluation and grading stress

explanation: Indirect experiences let you practice tricky situations safely so you feel ready when you step onto the real ward.

question: Why do circulating hormones only affect certain specific tissues rather than every cell in the body?

options.A: Only target cells possess the specific receptors for that hormone
options.B: Blood flow is completely blocked from non-target organs
options.C: Hormones are instantly destroyed if they touch wrong cells
options.D: Non-target cells actively repel circulating chemical messengers

explanation: A hormone travels everywhere via the blood, but only cells with matching receptors can receive the message and respond. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T9#GNS211_U1_T9_h1)

question: How can a nurse best support self-advocacy in a patient with a physical disability?

options.A: By making all medical and lifestyle decisions on behalf of the patient
options.B: By encouraging the patient to voice their own healthcare choices and rights
options.C: By shielding the patient from interacting with unfamiliar community members
options.D: By filing formal legal complaints without consulting the patient first

explanation: Self-advocacy grows when nurses empower patients to speak up and make their own informed decisions about care and life. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T9#GNS225_U5_T9_h8)

question: Where is the majority of the fluid in your body actually stored?

options.A: Inside the body cells
options.B: Within the lymphatic channels
options.C: Inside the blood vessels
options.D: Surrounding the tissue cells

explanation: Great job! Most of our body water is kept safely tucked away right inside our cells (intracellular fluid). Think of it as the main water reservoir of the body!

question: Why must a 24-hour emergency phone number be on hazardous material shipping documents?

options.A: To provide immediate expert guidance if a spill or exposure occurs
options.B: To let the receiving nurse ask about patient clinical history
options.C: To schedule the exact pickup time for the next laboratory batch
options.D: To allow the courier to confirm the payment receipt with accounting

explanation: If there's an accident on the road, emergency responders need someone to call instantly who knows how to handle that specific hazard safely.

question: Why is checking the publication date important when reading health articles online?

options.A: Older articles require special passwords to open them
options.B: Websites automatically delete articles after exactly one year
options.C: Older web pages take up too much space on computer screens
options.D: Medical guidelines and treatment practices change as new research emerges

explanation: Healthcare is fast-moving, and outdated information can lead to unsafe clinical practices or incorrect patient education. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T9#GNS113_U1_T9_h5)

question: What does the handy clinical acronym SBAR stand for?

options.A: Systolic, Blood, Airway, Respiration
options.B: Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation
options.C: Stabilization, Breathing, Analysis, Recovery
options.D: Safety, Beds, Ambulance, Response

explanation: SBAR is your best friend for quick, clear handovers. It helps you share the most important patient details without missing a beat.

question: What is the main goal of a two-way referral system in mental health care?

options.A: To permanently transfer all chronic clients to tertiary psychiatric hospitals
options.B: To reduce the total number of medications prescribed at primary clinics
options.C: To ensure smooth movement of clients and feedback between different levels of care
options.D: To allow primary nurses to independently diagnose complex psychiatric disorders

explanation: Think of a two-way referral as a team effort between clinics and big hospitals. It keeps communication flowing both ways so no patient is left stranded in the system!

question: How did early hospital-based training affect how nurses worked alongside doctors?

options.A: It created strict hierarchical traditions with medical officers
options.B: It completely removed the need for clinical supervision
options.C: It focused exclusively on advanced surgical techniques
options.D: It granted immediate university professorships to graduates

explanation: Spot on! The old hospital structures set up a very rigid setup where nurses were strictly subordinate to doctors, which modern training is helping to change.

question: Long-term hookworm infection most commonly leads to which major health problem?

options.A: Chronic kidney failure
options.B: Elevated blood pressure
options.C: Obstructive jaundice
options.D: Iron-deficiency anemia

explanation: Hookworms hook onto the intestinal wall and feed on blood, which over time causes significant blood loss and leads to iron-deficiency anemia.

question: Why should local numbing medicine with epinephrine be avoided when doing a biopsy right on the tip of the nose?

options.A: It makes the skin too soft for the punch blade to cut
options.B: It completely stops the local anesthetic from numbing the skin
options.C: It can cause severe restricted blood flow and tissue death
options.D: It reacts poorly with standard skin antiseptic solutions

explanation: Places like the nose tip have end-arteries with no backup blood supply. Adding epinephrine there can cut off circulation completely and cause the tissue to die (necrosis).

question: What two physical measurements are required to calculate a person's BMI?

options.A: Waist and hip measurements
options.B: Height and skinfold thickness
options.C: Height and weight
options.D: Weight and waist circumference

explanation: The standard BMI calculation relies exclusively on an individual's height and total body weight. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T10#GNS121_U1_T10_h2)

question: In public health, what does 'incidence' specifically measure?

options.A: The number of recovered patients discharged from a ward
options.B: The percentage of patients who die from a specific infection
options.C: The total number of people living with a chronic illness
options.D: The number of new cases of a disease over a specific period

explanation: Think of incidence as the brand-new cases popping up during a set time frame. You've got this!

question: What is a common management failure that lets unsafe injection habits keep happening?

options.A: Failing to provide safety training and discouraging near-miss reporting
options.B: Requiring doctors to supervise every single routine intramuscular injection
options.C: Enforcing strict handwashing rules during morning shift handovers
options.D: Providing too many sharps disposal containers in medication rooms

explanation: When hospitals punish people for speaking up or ignore close calls, hidden dangers stay on the ward waiting to cause actual harm.

question: What is the main goal of taking and handing over on the ward?

options.A: To transfer patient care responsibilities safely between shifts
options.B: To replace formal written patient medical records completely
options.C: To give nurses a chance to socialise before starting work
options.D: To allow doctors to check if nurses are doing their jobs

explanation: Handover makes sure that important care details move securely from the outgoing nurse to the incoming one, so no patient is left unprotected!

question: Why is ethical clearance and consent so important even in observational nursing studies?

options.A: To protect patient privacy and respect autonomy
options.B: To eliminate all possibilities of observer bias completely
options.C: To ensure the hospital receives more funding for research
options.D: To prevent the researcher from getting tired during shifts

explanation: Spot on! Even when we are just watching, we must always respect patients' privacy rights and personal autonomy.

question: Why is drying a newborn immediately after birth so crucial?

options.A: It washes away skin oils
options.B: It lowers their heart rate to normal
options.C: It stimulates breathing and keeps them warm
options.D: It stops baby jaundice from developing

explanation: Drying wipes away wet fluid so the baby doesn't get chilled from evaporation, and the rubbing action acts as a gentle nudge telling them to breathe!

question: Why do Nigerian healthcare facilities need a clear waste management plan and ongoing staff training?

options.A: To reduce the number of patients visiting outpatient departments
options.B: To bridge the gap between written safety policies and actual clinical practice
options.C: To eliminate the need for electricity in hospital laboratories
options.D: To qualify for international sports tournament sponsorships

explanation: Having a rulebook on paper isn't enough—training ensures everyone actually follows safe habits on the ward every single day!

question: Which quick bedside test should a nurse perform immediately for any patient presenting with sudden confusion?

options.A: Blood glucose test
options.B: Chest X-ray imaging
options.C: Electrocardiogram test
options.D: Complete blood count

explanation: Low blood sugar is a common, easily reversible cause of altered mental status that must be checked right away. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T2#GNS315_U2_T2_h6)

question: What is the core spiritual reason behind vegetarianism in many Hindu and Buddhist traditions?

options.A: Strict government mandates enforced by ancient rulers
options.B: Ahimsa, meaning non-violence toward all living creatures
options.C: The absence of livestock farming methods in early history
options.D: The belief that all animal proteins cause immediate physical disease

explanation: Ahimsa is the beautiful principle of avoiding harm to any living thing, which strongly guides plant-based eating habits in these traditions.

question: A hospital notices multiple incident reports about look-alike drug vials. What is the best quality improvement action?

options.A: Stop ordering that medication entirely without finding an alternative
options.B: Instruct all nurses to read medication labels three times before work
options.C: Fire the nurses who reported the confusing packaging
options.D: Change how and where those specific drug vials are stored

explanation: Brilliant! Fixing the system—like changing drug storage or packaging—is way more effective than just telling staff to 'be careful.'

question: How does a local food network protect your neighborhood during a transport strike?

options.A: By increasing the cost of basic food items
options.B: By providing a protective buffer of nearby food sources
options.C: By shutting down local markets immediately
options.D: By depending completely on imported supplies

explanation: Exactly! When long-distance transport is blocked, having food grown right in your backyard or nearby keeps everyone fed. Great thinking!

question: Why do hospitals love using cycle menus?

options.A: They provide variety while simplifying food purchasing and kitchen planning
options.B: They ensure that all meals are served at zero financial cost
options.C: They guarantee that every patient eats the exact same food forever
options.D: They allow the kitchen to completely avoid checking food expiration dates

explanation: Cycle menus keep patients from getting bored with food while helping the kitchen budget and buy supplies easily.

question: What is the main reason why female genital mutilation (FGM) is practiced?

options.A: Treating severe infections
options.B: Correcting birth defects
options.C: Preventing heavy menstrual bleeding
options.D: Non-medical reasons

explanation: FGM is done for cultural, traditional, or religious reasons—it has no health benefits at all. As nurses, knowing this helps us understand the social pressures our patients face.

question: What is the most important check for a nurse right after a patient returns from an upper scope (endoscopy)?

options.A: Lying them flat on their back for six hours
options.B: Checking that their gag reflex is back before giving water
options.C: Encouraging them to eat a heavy meal
options.D: Giving a laxative to clear out dye

explanation: Their throat was numbed for the procedure, so giving water too soon could cause it to go straight into their lungs. Always test that gag reflex first!

question: What is one of the main day-to-day duties of a nurse during antenatal clinic visits?

options.A: Prescribing permanent contraceptive sterilizations
options.B: Performing major surgical deliveries in the outpatient clinic
options.C: Conducting physical assessments and administering immunizations
options.D: Diagnosing rare genetic mutations in the laboratory

explanation: Correct! As a nurse, you'll check vital signs, monitor the baby's growth, and give essential vaccines like tetanus toxoid.

question: Why do we use Boolean words like AND and OR when searching research databases?

options.A: To automatically translate foreign language articles into English
options.B: To convert secondary research summaries into primary data tables
options.C: To check if the author of a research paper has a valid license
options.D: To narrow or broaden search results to find relevant articles

explanation: Great work! Words like AND and OR help you filter your search so you don't get drowned in millions of unrelated papers.

question: A patient with a head injury seems stable. Why must you keep monitoring them closely over the next few days?

options.A: Complications often develop hours or days after the primary injury
options.B: Hospital policies require discharges within 48 hours
options.C: Patients usually fake their symptoms to get more attention
options.D: Medications stop working completely after the first day

explanation: Brain swelling takes time to build up. A patient looking fine right now can take a sudden turn for the worse later, so constant watch is key!

question: Why are pregnant women and young children most vulnerable to harmful food myths?

options.A: They consume more processed foods than adults do
options.B: They have high nutritional demands for growth and development
options.C: They lack access to clean drinking water in all areas
options.D: They are legally required to follow traditional diets

explanation: Because their bodies need rich nutrients for rapid growth and pregnancy, restricting their diet can unfortunately lead to health setbacks.

question: What exactly is a 'sampling frame' in research?

options.A: The final group of patients selected for a clinical trial
options.B: The statistical formula used to calculate sample size
options.C: A physical list of all eligible members in a target population
options.D: A barrier preventing patients from joining a study

explanation: You got it! Think of the sampling frame as your actual register, directory, or database from which you pull your participants.

question: What is the primary purpose of HIV counselling?

options.A: To enable the client to cope with stress and make personal decisions
options.B: To force patients to reveal their status to family members immediately
options.C: To diagnose opportunistic infections without laboratory tests
options.D: To register patients for mandatory government employment schemes

explanation: HIV counselling provides a safe space for clients to process emotions and make informed choices about their health. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T8#GNS216_U6_T8_h1)

question: Why does the electrical signal pause briefly at the AV node during a heartbeat?

options.A: To equalize blood pressure between the left and right sides
options.B: To give the SA node time to recharge its chemical supply
options.C: To prevent the heart muscle from entering complete tetanus
options.D: To allow the atria time to empty blood into the ventricles

explanation: Great job thinking about heart mechanics! That brief pause at the AV node is super important—it makes sure the top chambers (atria) finish squeezing all their blood down before the bottom chambers contract. You've got this!

question: Which scenario is a classic example of indirect contact transmission?

options.A: Getting infected with malaria from a mosquito bite during the rainy season
options.B: Catching a cold after touching a shared pen that an infected coworker used
options.C: Developing a wound infection from direct contact with a draining sore
options.D: Inhaling large respiratory droplets expelled by someone coughing nearby

explanation: The shared pen acts as a fomite, transferring the virus indirectly from the coworker's hand to the new host's hand. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T6#GNS313_U1_T6_h4)

question: What does 'coffee-ground emesis' (vomit that looks like coffee grounds) usually tell you during an assessment?

options.A: There is a complete blockage in the lower colon
options.B: The patient took too many oral iron supplements with food
options.C: The pancreas is inflamed and backing up into the stomach
options.D: There is upper GI bleeding, and the blood has been sitting in stomach acid

explanation: When bleeding happens in the upper GI tract, stomach acid reacts with the hemoglobin in the blood, turning it dark and giving vomit that classic coffee-ground texture.

question: Where does the circulating nurse usually stay and work during a surgical operation?

options.A: Inside the sterile core wearing a gown and gloves
options.B: Directly beside the surgeon handing out instruments
options.C: At the head of the patient managing anesthesia equipment
options.D: Outside the sterile field in the unscrubbed area

explanation: The circulating nurse is unscrubbed and moves freely around the room to manage supplies, records, and non-sterile needs.

question: What do we mean when we say a bacterium has innate resistance?

options.A: It develops after a patient completes a full course of drugs
options.B: It is a natural, built-in characteristic of a bacterial species
options.C: It is acquired from other bacteria via horizontal gene transfer
options.D: It appears only when the patient has a weakened immune system

explanation: Innate means it was born that way! Some bacteria naturally have built-in defenses against certain drugs without ever needing prior exposure. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T92#GNS214_U1_T92_h3)

question: What is the main goal of injection safety in nursing?

options.A: To prevent harm to the patient, nurse, and community
options.B: To ensure medications dissolve faster in the bloodstream
options.C: To reduce the financial cost of hospital supplies
options.D: To speed up the delivery of emergency medications

explanation: You got this! Injection safety is all about protecting everyone from accidental injury or infection. Keeping patients, ourselves, and our communities safe always comes first.

question: What do we call the lifelong process of learning what society expects from males and females?

options.A: The legal right to vote regardless of a person's gender identity
options.B: The lifelong process of learning society's expectations for males and females
options.C: A medical procedure used to alter a person's biological sex characteristics
options.D: A hospital policy ensuring equal pay for male and female nurses

explanation: From childhood, family and society teach us how we are 'supposed' to act, dress, and behave based on our gender. That learning process is gender socialization!

question: What is the main goal of the science of improvement in healthcare?

options.A: Reducing hospital operational costs by cutting nursing staff numbers
options.B: Punishing staff members who make medication administration errors
options.C: Discovering entirely new medical treatments through laboratory trials
options.D: Applying proven knowledge to reliably improve daily care processes

explanation: Improvement science simply means taking what we already know works and finding practical, everyday ways to use it consistently in the ward. You've got this!

question: A newly delivered mother wants to take very hot baths to wash away her postpartum discharge (lochia). What key safety point should you share with her?

options.A: Hot water completely stops the normal production of breast milk
options.B: Heat causes vasodilation, which can potentially worsen postpartum bleeding
options.C: Heat causes immediate permanent blindness in newborns
options.D: Hot water freezes the uterine muscles, preventing involution

explanation: Remember, heat opens up blood vessels (vasodilation). For a new mum, this extra blood flow can actually cause her to bleed more than normal after delivery.

question: What medical term describes a constant ringing or buzzing sound in the ears?

options.A: Vertigo
options.B: Tinnitus
options.C: Otitis
options.D: Presbycusis

explanation: Tinnitus is a very common issue where a person hears phantom sounds like ringing or buzzing when no external sound is actually there.

question: How long can a released egg survive and remain ready for fertilization?

options.A: 12 to 24 hours
options.B: 1 week
options.C: Up to 1 month
options.D: 3 to 5 days

explanation: The egg has a very short window of about 12 to 24 hours after ovulation to meet a sperm cell. Timing is everything!

question: What kind of organism causes paragonimiasis?

options.A: A lung fluke
options.B: A blood parasite
options.C: A tissue bacterium
options.D: A roundworm

explanation: You got this! Paragonimiasis is caused by flatworms called lung flukes. Think of them as tiny parasites that love to settle down in the respiratory system.

question: What does a community action plan typically include?

options.A: A list of punishments for community members who refuse care
options.B: Detailed medical histories of every nurse in the clinic
options.C: Financial statements of international donor agencies
options.D: Objectives, assigned tasks, timelines, and success indicators

explanation: An action plan provides a clear roadmap showing who will do what, when, and how success will be measured. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T5#GNS124_U4_T5_h6)

question: What is the main goal of a public-private partnership (PPP) in healthcare?

options.A: To combine government resources with private sector investment and efficiency
options.B: To ensure that private companies take full control of national health policy
options.C: To completely transfer government health responsibilities to private owners
options.D: To eliminate all out-of-pocket costs for vulnerable patient populations

explanation: Think of a PPP as teamwork! The government teams up with private companies to bring in extra funds and better management, making health systems stronger together.

question: Why is a 'blameless' reporting culture so good for hospital safety?

options.A: It encourages workers to report errors honestly without fear
options.B: It excuses careless healthcare workers from facing legal consequences
options.C: It allows hospital management to ignore minor documentation errors
options.D: It proves to patients that nurses never make mistakes

explanation: Exactly! When we remove the fear of victimization, staff feel safe to speak up, giving management the real data needed to fix broken systems.

question: Why do we view disaster management as an endless cycle rather than a straight line?

options.A: Because recovery takes the exact same amount of time as mitigation
options.B: Because lessons learned during recovery directly inform future mitigation and preparedness
options.C: Because disasters always happen at the exact same time every year
options.D: Because emergency personnel never stop responding to disasters

explanation: Brilliant! Every time we recover from a disaster, we learn valuable lessons that help us get better prepared for the next one.

question: What is the main benefit of community-based rehabilitation (CBR)?

options.A: It completely stops patients from ever visiting a hospital
options.B: It removes the need for support from family members
options.C: It brings healthcare services right into the patient's local environment
options.D: It focuses only on surgical procedures

explanation: You got it! CBR makes care super accessible because it meets patients where they live, making it easier for them to join in and transition back to everyday life.

question: A patient newly diagnosed with celiac disease is stressed about grocery shopping. What is your best first step as a nurse?

options.A: Advise the patient to avoid eating all packaged foods forever.
options.B: Refer the patient immediately to a psychiatric inpatient facility.
options.C: Provide a strict list of expensive specialty imported commercial snacks.
options.D: Teach the patient how to identify naturally gluten-free whole foods and read labels.

explanation: Empowering patients with label-reading skills and showing them naturally safe whole foods builds confidence and reduces anxiety!

question: Why do doctors use a combination of different chemotherapy drugs instead of just one?

options.A: To completely eliminate all side effects
options.B: To target only upper-body lymph nodes
options.C: To finish the entire treatment in a single afternoon
options.D: To attack cancer cells through different angles and prevent drug resistance

explanation: Using a combo team of drugs hits the cancer from multiple directions, making it much harder for the sneaky cancer cells to find a way to resist.

question: A patient's pulse oximeter shows 82%, but they are talking and breathing easily. What should you do first?

options.A: Turn off the monitor because it is definitely broken
options.B: Immediately start chest compressions and call a code blue
options.C: Check the physical patient and look for cold fingers or nail polish
options.D: Assume the patient is in severe respiratory distress

explanation: Always assess your patient before the machine! Poor circulation or dark nail polish often causes false low readings. Great nursing instinct!

question: A patient's mother-in-law says she shouldn't eat eggs or the baby will be born hairless. How should you, as the nurse, respond?

options.A: Agree with the cultural belief to avoid causing family tension
options.B: Tell the patient to ignore her family completely and eat in secret
options.C: Prescribe an expensive chemical supplement to replace the eggs
options.D: Respectfully explain that eggs are a safe, rich source of protein and essential nutrients

explanation: Well done! Always respect family and culture, but gently guide patients toward safe, nutritious truths without sounding rude.

question: What is the main advantage of using the IMCI strategy when treating sick children?

options.A: It looks at the whole child and evaluates multiple overlapping symptoms
options.B: It focuses exclusively on treating severe surgical emergencies
options.C: It replaces the need for any laboratory testing in rural clinics
options.D: It removes the need for nurses to talk with caregivers

explanation: You're doing great! IMCI helps you assess the whole child because sick kids often suffer from more than one issue at the same time.

question: Why is it useful for a practicing nurse to know a bit about health economics?

options.A: It allows them to audit hospital financial accounts directly
options.B: It replaces the need for clinical nursing assessments
options.C: It grants them legal power to set national drug prices
options.D: It helps them advocate for efficient resource use and fair compensation

explanation: Understanding how resources and money flow helps you manage bedside supplies wisely and speak up for better working conditions and patient care.

question: Why is maintaining good musculoskeletal health so important for a patient?

options.A: It prevents all forms of infectious diseases
options.B: It completely stops the natural aging process
options.C: It preserves daily mobility and personal independence
options.D: It lowers the patient's blood pressure levels

explanation: Healthy bones, joints, and muscles allow a person to move freely and care for themselves without relying on others. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T25#GNS222_U1_T25_h1)

question: Why do close contacts of a meningitis patient get given preventive (prophylactic) antibiotics?

options.A: To cut down hospital bills in the community
options.B: To clear the bacteria from their nose and throat and stop it from spreading
options.C: To cure unrelated infections they might have
options.D: To boost their immunity against all viruses

explanation: Giving quick preventive meds to family members or close contacts clears the bacteria out of their upper airway before it can make them sick or pass it to someone else.

question: How do we tell an indirect obstetric cause of maternal death apart from a direct one?

options.A: It has no relation to the female reproductive system at all
options.B: It only happens during the third trimester of labor
options.C: It is exclusively caused by surgical errors
options.D: It is caused by a pre-existing medical condition worsened by pregnancy

explanation: Spot on! Indirect causes are medical issues like heart disease or severe malaria that were already there, but got dangerously worse because of the physical changes of pregnancy.

question: What is the main goal of vestibular rehabilitation therapy?

options.A: To permanently eliminate all physical movement of the head
options.B: To train the central nervous system to compensate for inner ear deficits
options.C: To surgically replace the delicate structures of the inner ear
options.D: To increase blood pressure and prevent fainting episodes

explanation: Spot on! Vestibular therapy uses smart exercises to help the brain learn how to handle balance signals better, even if the inner ear isn't working at 100%.

question: Which symptom is most common in nurses who spend long hours staring at computer screens for charting?

options.A: Numbness in the big toes
options.B: Swelling of the lower legs
options.C: Weakness in the handgrip
options.D: Dry and fatigued eyes

explanation: You got it! When we stare at screens, we tend to blink less, which leaves our eyes feeling dry and tired. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h6)

question: A patient recovering from a thyroidectomy feels numb and tingling around their lips and fingers. What is the likely cause?

options.A: Temporary damage to the recurrent laryngeal nerve
options.B: Accidental hypocalcemia from parathyroid gland injury
options.C: Severe postoperative hemorrhage behind the incision
options.D: Early warning signs of an impending thyroid storm

explanation: You nailed it! The tiny parathyroid glands sit right near the thyroid and can get nudged during surgery, causing calcium levels to drop and fingers/lips to tingle.

question: Which of these is NOT a recommended strategy for community nurses working in areas with traditional healing systems?

options.A: Advocating for the human rights of confined patients
options.B: Facilitating safe referrals to psychiatric facilities
options.C: Educating healers to spot severe mental illness signs
options.D: Condemning and mocking local cultural beliefs openly

explanation: You got this! Mocking cultural beliefs alienates the community and drives patients far away from seeking professional help. Always lead with respect.

question: Which body membrane lines closed internal cavities that do NOT open to the outside?

options.A: Synovial membrane
options.B: Mucous membrane
options.C: Serous membrane
options.D: Cutaneous membrane

explanation: Serous membranes line closed cavities like your chest and abdomen, making a slippery fluid to cut down friction.

question: Which of these is NOT a common mistake when setting objectives?

options.A: Creating vague statements without metrics
options.B: Consulting frontline staff during the drafting phase
options.C: Setting too many objectives at once
options.D: Setting targets in isolation from the team

explanation: Talking to your staff is a fantastic practice, not a mistake! The other choices are classic pitfalls to avoid.

question: What is the main purpose of defibulation surgery in an FGM-affected woman?

options.A: To open fused scar tissue and restore normal drainage and function
options.B: To enhance the speed of weight loss
options.C: To permanently stop menstrual bleeding
options.D: To prevent future pelvic bone fractures

question: A teenage girl living in extreme poverty begins a relationship with an older man who pays her school fees and buys her food in exchange for sex. Which primary driver is influencing this behavior?

options.A: Personal invulnerability to infections
options.B: Socioeconomic hardship and survival needs
options.C: Normal adolescent brain maturation
options.D: Peer pressure from school classmates

question: What simple home care helps most with scrotal swelling on the first day after surgery?

options.A: Massaging the scrotum gently to drain excess fluid
options.B: Applying an ice pack wrapped in a cloth intermittently
options.C: Taking a long soak in a warm bathtub twice a day
options.D: Applying a firm heating pad directly to the skin

question: You tally up the oral pills dispensed for the month and notice the total is higher than the actual stock used. What is your best first step?

options.A: Cross-check the daily registers and tally sheets again to find counting errors
options.B: Submit the higher number anyway to show high community demand
options.C: Report the pharmaceutical company for supplying fewer tablets than stated
options.D: Discard the tally sheets and invent new numbers that match the stock balance

explanation: Exactly right! Always review your source documents first to track down where a simple addition or tally mistake happened.

question: What is almost always the very first test a nurse or doctor will order for a woman of childbearing age with secondary amenorrhoea?

options.A: Brain MRI
options.B: Endometrial biopsy
options.C: Karyotype analysis
options.D: Pregnancy test

question: What type of cleaning technique should a nurse use for skeletal traction pin sites?

options.A: Routine household washing
options.B: Clean technique
options.C: Sterile technique
options.D: Surgical scrubbing without gloves

explanation: Because those pins go straight into the bone, keeping things sterile is a must to stop germs from causing a bone infection.

question: Why are alternative rites of passage considered effective grassroots strategies against FGM?

options.A: They replace traditional ceremonies with strict western religious rituals
options.B: They preserve cultural celebrations of maturity while eliminating physical harm
options.C: They allow traditional cutters to continue practicing safely in hospitals
options.D: They provide direct employment for healthcare workers in rural clinics

explanation: Alternative rites honor the cultural need for a coming-of-age milestone while removing the dangerous physical cutting component. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T7#GNS312_U1_T7_h4)

question: Which part of the cerebellar peduncle mainly sends outgoing motor correction signals away from the cerebellum?

options.A: Posterior cerebellar peduncle

options.C: Superior cerebellar peduncle
